text.p: Georgia's General Assembly has approved an $11.7 billion budget that raises teacher salaries by six percent and boosts other state workers' pay by four percent.

The budget for the year beginning July 1 was approved 157-17 in the House and 48-5 in the Senate late last week. Earlier in the session, the legislature adopted a $452 million supplemental budget that raised spending to $11.7 billion for fiscal 1997, which ends June 30.

Together, the two budgets authorize $587.5 million of general obligation bonds, mainly for schools and highway projects. That would put Georgia's outstanding debt at $5.5 billion, or about half of its constitutional limit.
Gov. Zell Miller had sought the teacher pay hikes for the third consecutive year as part of a four-year plan to make Georgia education salaries the highest in the Southeast.
Miller's press spokesman said the governor was still reviewing the budget on Monday and had not indicated whether he would veto any major projects.

Before adjourning late Friday night, the General Assembly also approved a welfare reform plan that cuts off most benefits after four years, and adopted legislation allowing the state to seize the assets of people who commit Medicaid fraud.
